title: Good chest day vs Bad chest day
summary: NH argues a bad chest day only trains chest with stacked junk volume, while a good chest day trains chest as a byproduct of a synergistic upper day: one or two heavy presses, shoulders, triceps, rows and supersets. For natural lifters he favors chest frequency of 2-3x/week with 2-3 quality sets over one big weekly session.
claims: A bad chest day trains only chest; a good chest day trains chest as a byproduct within a synergistic upper day
Bro splits that train one muscle per day are a waste of time for natural lifters
Stacking as many chest exercises as possible into a template does not build a bigger chest
Chest synergizes with shoulders and triceps, so pair them (gentleman split logic based on muscle pairings)
25 sets for chest is junk volume: 60-70% of the reps do nothing because they are not challenging or the chest is already spent
Intensity and breaking down fibers build muscle, not the pump; a program can give no pump and still grow you
For chest use one big press, maybe a second press or accessory, and maybe one isolation; more is pointless
Doing four heavy chest compounds in one session forces you to sandbag intensity just to survive the workout
The bench press grew his chest, but it is not the only horizontal press
Dips are in many ways superior to the bench for hypertrophy but carry slightly higher shoulder injury risk if done poorly
The best chest movement is the one you enjoy and can do for a long time; if the bench injures you every four months, drop it
Weighted push-ups work; calisthenics athletes have big chests at light bodyweights
Add a vertical press, rows and upper back work to chest day; your back is visible from the front too
Your chest may be limited by neglected areas such as arm strength and size or shoulder health
2-3 sets per session is plenty for chest; naturals should prioritize frequency over volume
Training chest 2-3 times a week with less volume and more precise intensity beats one weekly chest day
Keep reps in the tank so you can train again in 2-3 days; repeatability is the bread and butter of natural bodybuilding, and a lift you can only do every 15 days is not a good lift
Beginners can start with one chest movement, one vertical press and one biceps movement, then progressively add exercises
Good upper days have many exercises; good lower days are more minimalist because upper body has more small muscles to isolate
You can even superset calves on a chest or upper day
If you are out of breath after a set of bench, lose weight and work on your heart and lungs
Superset a press with a row (e.g. bench plus dumbbell row) for free upper back tonnage
You don't need five minutes of rest for chest; fill the downtime with another exercise instead of your phone
Small muscles recover very fast, so superset them liberally and back off only if you feel it's too much
Drop sets artificially lower intensity and drift into junk volume; a good 3x6-10 works perfectly well
Spread chest work through the week, e.g. ring push-ups, ring flies or close-grip bench on an arm day
Frequent chest training gives fresher, higher-quality tonnage and lower injury risk; pec injuries mostly hit once-a-week bro-splitters
Bad template (description): bench 5x10-15, dips 3xAMRAP, flies 4x15-20, cable flies 5x10-12, push-ups 5xAMRAP leads to long downtime and junk volume

Good template (description): bench/dips/weighted push-ups 3x6-10 + rows 3x8-12; OHP 4x6-12 + French press/skull-crushers 4x8-12 + laterals or finger curls 4x10-15; DB press/decline push-ups/flies 3x10-15 + weighted chin-ups 3x5 + crunches 3xAMRAP
He built a thick chest largely with push-ups and bench early on and now only maintains it
